{{Current events|year=2019|month=11|day=28|content=

<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Allied Democratic Forces insurgency]]
**An attack on an [[United Nations]] center in the Congo by [[Mai-Mai]] militants kills three [[Ebola]] response workers and a police officer. [https://www.latimes.com/world-nation/story/2019-11-28/ebola-responders-congo-world-health-organization (''LA Times'')]
**The death toll in November attacks by [[Islamist]] militants in the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] increases to 107 from violence in and around [[Beni, Democratic Republic of the Congo|Beni]] since November 5. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/11/dr-congo-brink-191127120254060.html (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.trtworld.com/africa/democratic-republic-of-congo-massacre-death-toll-rises-to-27-31773 (TRT World)]
*[[2019 Iraqi protests]]
**In one of the deadliest days of the protests so far, [[Iraq]]i security forces open fire and kill 25 people who were blocking a bridge in [[Nasiriyah]], while 10 people are killed in [[Najaf]], and four people are shot dead in the capital [[Baghdad]]. The [[Iraqi Armed Forces]] says an emergency unit had been created to "impose security and restore order" in response to the violence. 45 people have been killed by security forces in total. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-middle-east-50584123 (BBC)] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/nov/29/iraq-in-turmoil-as-45-shot-dead-by-security-forces-in-protests (''The Guardian'')]
*Two [[Turkish Armed Forces|Turkish troops]] are killed by [[Mortar (weapon)|mortar fire]] in the [[Akçakale]] district of Turkey, near the [[Syria–Turkey border|Syrian border]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/turkey/mortar-attack-martyrs-2-soldiers-in-turkeys-southeast/1657859 (AA)]
*[[South Korea]]n [[Republic of Korea Army|army]] officials claim that [[North Korea]] launched two projectiles "from a super-large caliber multiple rocket launcher." [https://www.cnn.com/2019/11/28/asia/north-korea-launch-intl-hnk/index.html (CNN)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2019 Albania earthquake]]
**Twenty more bodies are found under destroyed buildings after the earthquake in [[Albania]] two days ago, bringing the death toll to 50 people. [https://shqiptarja.com/lajm/40-viktima-nga-termeti-nxirren-te-gjithe-personat-nga-rrenojat-ne-thumane-vijojne-kerkimet-ne-durres-per-6-persona (Shqiptarja.com)]

;Health and environment
*[[2019 Samoa measles outbreak]]
**The [[United Nations]] blames [[anti-vaccination]] messages for the current outbreak of [[measles]] in the Pacific island nation, where the death toll has risen to 39 and is expected to rise as 200 are reported hospitalised, according to the [[World Health Organization]]. Total cases now soar to near 3,000. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/nov/28/samoa-measles-outbreak-who-blames-anti-vaccine-scare-death-toll (''The Guardian'')] [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/404352/samoa-measles-epidemic-death-toll-reaches-39 (RNZ)]

;International relations
*[[Foreign relations of Benin]]
**The [[government of Benin]] orders [[List of ambassadors of the European Union|EU ambassador]] Oliver Nette to leave the country after accusing him of "meddling in their [[internal affairs]]". [https://www.dw.com/en/benin-orders-eu-ambassador-to-leave-reports/a-51441422 (DW)]
*[[Foreign relations of Bolivia]], [[Foreign relations of Israel]]
**[[Bolivia]] and [[Israel]] reestablish diplomatic relations after Bolivia suspended ties over a decade ago as a consequence of [[Operation Cast Lead]]. The foreign minister of the [[2019 Bolivian political crisis#Assumption of presidency by Jeanine_Áñez|Bolivian transitional government]] says [[President of Bolivia|President]] [[Evo Morales]] took the decision in 2009 "without thinking about the economic and commercial consequences". [https://www.jpost.com/Israel-News/Bolivia-renews-ties-with-Israel-609316 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]

;Law and crime
*[[Censorship in Vietnam]]
**In the third case this month, and the second this week, a court in [[Vietnam]] convicts and sentences a [[Facebook]] user to nine years in prison for defaming the ruling [[Communist Party of Vietnam|Communist Party]] and [[Government of Vietnam|government]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-vietnam-security-trials/vietnam-jails-third-activist-this-month-in-crackdown-on-facebook-posts-idUSKBN1Y20J3 (Reuters)]
*[[Hillsborough disaster]]
**[[David Duckenfield]], the former [[South Yorkshire Police]] [[chief superintendent]] who was in charge of the [[1988–89 FA Cup]] semi-final match between [[Liverpool F.C.]] and [[Nottingham Forest F.C.]] at [[Hillsborough Stadium]], is cleared of [[Manslaughter|manslaughter by gross negligence]] relating to the deaths of 96 Liverpool fans who were crushed to death during the match. The verdict sparks outrage from the families of victims. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-50592077 (BBC)] [https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2019/nov/28/hillsborough-families-outraged-david-duckenfield-not-guilty-verdict (''The Guardian'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019 Hong Kong protests]], [[Hong Kong–United Kingdom relations]]
**Following the [[Hong Kong Human Rights and Democracy Act|U.S. legislation regarding Hong Kong]], [[pro-democracy]] activist [[Joshua Wong]] urges [[Western nations]], especially the [[United Kingdom]], to "stand with Hong Kong" and calls for the penalization of leader [[Carrie Lam]]. [https://federalnewsnetwork.com/world-news/2019/11/protester-warns-against-police-moving-into-hong-kong-campus/ (Federal News Network)]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)]], [[Afghanistan–United States relations]]
**[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] and [[First Lady of the United States|First Lady]] [[Melania Trump]] make an unannounced [[Thanksgiving (United States)|Thanksgiving]] visit to troops at the [[Bagram Airfield]] in [[Afghanistan]], their second visit to a combat zone since taking office. While there he also claims he has re-started talks with the [[Taliban]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2019/11/28/us/politics/trump-afghanistan.html (''The New York Times'')]
